heavy-menstrual-bleeding.question: What are the treatment options for heavy menstrual bleeding?
heavy-menstrual-bleeding.summary: Non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), anti‑fibrinolytics, and paracetamol are medication classes used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding associated with IUD use [F1]. Specific endometrial ablation techniques evaluated include transcervical endometrial resection (TCRE) with or without rollerball, other resectoscopic endometrial ablation, microwave non‑resectoscopic endometrial ablation (NREA), hydrothermal ablation NREA, bipolar NREA, balloon NREA, and other NREA [F2]. Vitamin B1 was used as a treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding in copper IUD users [F3]. Medication classes used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding include non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), antifibrinolytics (tranexamic acid), combined oral contraceptives, combined vaginal ring, long‑cycle and luteal oral progestogens, levonorgestrel‑releasing intrauterine system, ethamsylate, and danazol [F4].

sub_answers.question: What medication classes are used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding?
sub_answers.answer: Non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), anti‑fibrinolytics, and paracetamol are medication classes used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding associated with IUD use [F1]. Vitamin B1 was used as a treatment for heavy menstrual bleeding in copper IUD users [F3]. Medication classes used to treat heavy menstrual bleeding include non‑steroidal anti‑inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs), antifibrinolytics (tranexamic acid), combined oral contraceptives, combined vaginal ring, long‑cycle and luteal oral progestogens, levonorgestrel‑releasing intrauterine system, ethamsylate, and danazol [F4]. Heavy bleeding caused by problems with ovulation, endometriosis, PCOS, and fibroids often can be managed with certain hormonal birth control methods [F6]. Hormone therapy can be helpful for heavy menstrual bleeding that occurs during perimenopause [F7]. Gonadotropin-releasing hormone (GnRH) agonists stop the menstrual cycle and reduce the size of fibroids [F8].

sub_answers.question: What surgical and procedural interventions are available for heavy menstrual bleeding?
sub_answers.answer: Specific endometrial ablation techniques evaluated include transcervical endometrial resection (TCRE) with or without rollerball, other resectoscopic endometrial ablation, microwave non‑resectoscopic endometrial ablation (NREA), hydrothermal ablation NREA, bipolar NREA, balloon NREA, and other NREA [F2]. Surgical and procedural interventions for heavy menstrual bleeding include open (abdominal), minimally invasive (vaginal or laparoscopic), and unspecified hysterectomy, resectoscopic endometrial ablation (REA), non‑resectoscopic endometrial ablation (NREA), unspecified endometrial ablation, and the levonorgestrel‑releasing intrauterine system [F5]. Hysterectomy is surgical removal of the uterus. Hysterectomy is used to treat fibroids and adenomyosis when other types of treatment have failed or are not an option [F9]. Uterine artery embolization (UAE) is used to treat fibroids by blocking the blood vessels to the uterus [F10]. Endometrial ablation destroys the lining of the uterus to stop or reduce menstrual bleeding [F11].
